headline: Batteries that store four hours of power are now cheaper than the open-cycle gas turbines favoured by many data centre developers in all 43 markets Wood Mackenzie surveyed, the consultancy says.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: new report on 9 Oct 2026 with a clear, wide finding; it is one consultancy's analysis relayed by one outlet.
importance_line: Power buyers and utilities could face lower costs if batteries replace gas peaking plants, which could in time reach households through electricity prices, but these are one consultancy's cost estimates.
summary: TechCrunch reports that the energy consultancy Wood Mackenzie found four-hour batteries cheaper than open-cycle gas turbines, a type of gas plant many data centre developers favour, in every one of the 43 markets it surveyed. Data centre developers buying every turbine they can find have pushed turbine prices up, with open-cycle units taking two to four years to procure and closed-cycle waiting lists running into the early 2030s.
notes: Wood Mackenzie's own report was not opened; figures are as relayed by TechCrunch.
